images.title: Nearest hundred and nearest thousand of 6,731
images.purpose: Show the same rabbit on two roads, one with the neighbouring hundreds and one with the neighbouring thousands, so the two nearest numbers can be different.
images.composition: Two roads stacked one above the other, each with two carrots, a halfway tick and the rabbit, and a jump arrow to each carrot under the road.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas with two horizontal roads, one above the other, each a thick flat bar in #2B2B2B spanning most of the width, with an equal margin at the left and right. On each road a carrot (amber #E69F00, green #009E73 leaf) stands at the left end and at the right end, and each road has exactly 4 tick marks: the two ends, a taller grey #6B7280 halfway tick at the middle, and a taller #CC79A7 tick for the rabbit. Each road has one flat grey rabbit in a mid hop just above its rabbit tick. All number labels sit above the road. TOP ROAD: labels 6,700 (left carrot), 6,750 (halfway tick), 6,731 (rabbit tick, just under one third of the way along the road from the left end), 6,800 (right carrot). Under the road two flat arrows start at the rabbit tick: a teal #0072B2 arrow to the left carrot with the text 31 jumps under it, and a grey #6B7280 arrow to the right carrot with the text 69 jumps under it. The left carrot has a #CC79A7 ring and the tag nearest hundred above its label. BOTTOM ROAD: labels 6,000 (left carrot), 6,500 (halfway tick), 6,731 (rabbit tick, just under three quarters of the way along the road from the left end), 7,000 (right carrot). Under the road two flat arrows start at the rabbit tick: a grey #6B7280 arrow to the left carrot with the text 731 jumps under it, and a teal #0072B2 arrow to the right carrot with the text 269 jumps under it. The right carrot has a #CC79A7 ring and the tag nearest thousand above its label. Nothing else is drawn.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: One number has its own nearest hundred and its own nearest thousand, and the two can be on different sides.
images.description: The rabbit at 6,731 on a hundreds road and on a thousands road, with the jumps to both neighbours on each, so the nearest hundred is 6,700 and the nearest thousand is 7,000.
images.context: Starting point is the chapter's two pictures of the rabbit between neighbouring hundreds and between neighbouring thousands, each with its halfway mark. The numbers are the plan's own from the concept's worked example: 6,731 with 31 and 69 jumps on the hundreds road and 731 and 269 jumps on the thousands road. The halfway marks 6,750 and 6,500 are computed. The label 6,731 is printed twice, once on each road.
images.teaching_notes: Read the top road first, then the bottom. The rabbit is near the left carrot on the top road and near the right carrot on the bottom road, so the answers are 6,700 and 7,000. Misconceptions M_ROUND_UP and M_NEAR_FAR.

image_decisions.why: Two stacked roads with counted jumps show that each line has its own two neighbours and its own nearest number.
